old_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene of a forest fire at dusk or early evening. The sky is tinged with hues of pink and purple, suggesting the time of day. Smoke billows thickly from the ground, partially obscuring the trees and creating an eerie atmosphere. The forest floor is scorched black, indicating the intensity of the fire. Flames are visible on the right side of the frame, with sparks and embers flying into the air, adding to the chaotic nature of the scene. The trees stand tall and mostly bare, their branches reaching upwards, some still holding onto their leaves. The smoke drifts slowly across the landscape, creating a sense of movement and progression. The overall mood is one of destruction and the relentless power of nature. There are no animals or people present in the video, focusing solely on the natural elements and the aftermath of the fire. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to absorb the full extent of the devastation.

caption: The video captures a wide, smoke-hazed landscape of a recently burned field beneath a pale pink sky. Blackened ground fills the foreground, studded with thin dead saplings, while taller, partly leafless trees rise across the midground and right. A low layer of white smoke hangs over the charred field and shifts subtly in density from frame to frame. Small active flames already burn in two places: a bright patch at the bottom-center foreground and a longer line of fire tracing the right edge. Throughout the excerpt the right-side line of fire continues to flicker and smolder, remaining visible until the last frame. The bottom-center flame gradually weakens and shrinks, drifting toward the lower edge as the view slowly tightens. This tightening enlarges the central and right-side trees while pushing the foreground flame out of the bottom of the frame. The pinkish sky and haze stay essentially constant in color and brightness across the sequence. A faint watermark sits in the lower right corner. The scene presents an ongoing burn aftermath rather than a completed action, with fire still active on the right as the foreground patch fades from view.

This clip is a temporally cropped excerpt, with arbitrary start and end boundaries. It is NOT
necessarily a complete action and it is NOT a loop. Describe the visible portion of a process
without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
